raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Sweep plots can now filter string values containing comparison operators. For example, `label!=build==one` selects every other label instead of trying to read a column named `label!=build`.

## Claims

- Parse the first comparison operator and preserve the complete target string, including repeated or leading `==`.
- Keep the existing numeric, infinity, and multiple-filter behavior.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_plot_filters.py --confcutdir=tests/benchmarks -q`: the three added regression cases failed on the unchanged parser, with 27 existing tests passing; the final change passes all 30. Tests invoke the real `PlotFilters` parser and apply it to pandas data. The scoped command omits the global GPU fixtures.

Scoped native Linux pre-commit hooks pass, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, and Buildkite test tethering. The existing `Benchmarks CLI` lane already runs `tests/benchmarks/`.

The submitting human reviewed every changed line and initiated the same test command through the review window; all 30 tests passed. Model evaluation is unnecessary for this CPU plot-filter parser; no model, serving engine, or GPU execution was tested.

## Details

The previous parser searched operator types in a fixed order and split every occurrence. An `==` inside the target could win over the earlier `!=`, or repeated `==` could raise an unpacking error. Split once at the first complete comparison token, preserving longer tokens before `<` and `>`.

Duplicate checks on October 7 searched open PRs for `PlotFilterBase` and plot/filter symptoms and inspected matching file patches. #55698 changes figure grouping and #55664 changes worker-result collection; neither changes filter parsing. This is independent of our sweep-name and JSON-list PRs #60328/#60329.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used for diagnosis, implementation, tests, and this description.

</details>

I'm preparing a separate quoted-comma filter fix and checked that it does not duplicate this PR.

For example, `_benchmark_name=="fp8,tp2",request_rate>1` still fails because `PlotFilters.parse_str` splits every comma, including commas inside a quoted target. This change leaves `PlotFilterBase` and comparison-operator selection untouched; it only changes how expressions are separated and rejects unterminated quoted values.

Validation: the original production code gives 6 failures / 36 passes; the patched suite passes all 42 cases, including real CLI filtering and literal apostrophe/backslash compatibility.

Branch: https://github.com/singh4jitendra/vllm/tree/fix/bench-quoted-filter-values

Opened upstream PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63469

files.patch:
@@ -158,6 +158,19 @@ def test_parse_str_inf_edge_case(self):
         assert filter_obj.var == "request_rate"
         assert filter_obj.target == "inf"
 
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "filter_str,expected",
+        [
+            ("label==build==one", ["build==one"]),
+            ("label!=build==one", ["==preview", "other"]),
+            ("label====preview", ["==preview"]),
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_string_target_preserves_operator_characters(self, filter_str, expected):
+        df = pd.DataFrame({"label": ["build==one", "==preview", "other"]})
+        filtered = PlotFilters.parse_str(filter_str).apply(df)
+        assert filtered["label"].tolist() == expected
+
     def test_parse_multiple_filters(self):
         """Test parsing multiple filters."""
         filters = PlotFilters.parse_str("request_rate>5.0,value<=40")

@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@
 from types import TracebackType
 from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, ClassVar, Self
 
+import regex as re
 from typing_extensions import override
 
 from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
@@ -29,18 +30,15 @@ class PlotFilterBase(ABC):
 
     @classmethod
     def parse_str(cls, s: str):
-        for op_key in PLOT_FILTERS:
-            if op_key in s:
-                key, value = s.split(op_key)
-                return PLOT_FILTERS[op_key](
-                    key,
-                    value.removeprefix(op_key).strip("'").strip('"'),
-                )
-        else:
-            raise ValueError(
-                f"Invalid operator for plot filter '{s}'. "
-                f"Valid operators are: {sorted(PLOT_FILTERS)}",
-            )
+        parts = re.split(r"(==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)", s, maxsplit=1)
+        if len(parts) == 3:
+            key, op_key, value = parts
+            return PLOT_FILTERS[op_key](key, value.strip("'").strip('"'))
+
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Invalid operator for plot filter '{s}'. "
+            f"Valid operators are: {sorted(PLOT_FILTERS)}",
+        )
 
     @abstractmethod
     def apply(self, df: "pd.DataFrame") -> "pd.DataFrame":
